newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, May hits 7-1/2 month high.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, May hits 7-1/2 month high.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures held most of their early gains to close stronger across the board on Wednesday.

Benchmark May gapped higher at the open and climbed to the highest level since August 22. It closed up 30 stg at 1,047 stg per tonne, slightly off the session high of 1,050 due to light profit-taking and origin selling to hedge new crops, especially in back-months, traders said.

Though New York prices slipped $19 to $1,493 per tonne by 1624 GMT on profit-taking, New York's stellar performance on Tuesday sparked a cocoa rally that sent nearby CSCE cocoa futures up through key technical levels and to 2-1/2 year highs.
Traders attributed initial price rises to short-covering. That, they said, led to a shattering of key resistance levels and attracted new speculative long positions.
Broker GNI said nearby CSCE cocoa futures had "an upside break out of the perfect pennant formation" and expected more gains.
Cocoa was also seen benefitting from recent steep declines in global stock markets, led by the U.S. At 1500 GMT, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 58.16 index points at 6553.89.
Stock weakness may have forced some funds to shift money into commodities, which could also explain firmness in the Commodity Research Bureau's index, a trader said.

Despite expectations for more near-term gains, traders and analysts remained wary. They said fundamentals did not justify cocoa's strength, especially amid expectations for a large Ivorian crop and a fall in European grinds.
European grind data are expected within a week and analysts in Amsterdam said on Wednesday that grindings could fall. However, they said demand still looked steady to higher.
Some technical traders were also sidelined.
Agricultural analyst Barry Rosen said in a daily commentary "we do not see a good risk/reward for being a buyer so, we will stand aside and wait."

Using charts on New York cocoa futures, he said "with a five-wave (Elliot) wave pattern complete on the next high, we may get more consolidation before we take-off to higher numbers into the May time window."
Cocoa volume on LIFFE tallied 8,063 contracts on Wednesday.
